title: Shopify orders to Google Sheets | 50agents
description: To send Shopify orders to Google Sheets, add a row per new order with its items and total, or one row per item. Captain sets it up from one sentence.

h2.how: How to send Shopify orders to Google Sheets
h2.compare: Other ways to send Shopify orders to Google Sheets

answer: To send Shopify orders to Google Sheets, tell Captain "Set up an automation: every new Shopify order is added as a row to my Google Sheet".
It builds an automation that writes only to your sheet, so nothing needs approval.

steps.title: You say it, and pick the row shape
steps.body: Tell Captain if you want one row per order or one per item. It asks which sheet to use.

steps.title: Captain shows you the plan
steps.body: New Order starts it, the line items are listed, and Add New Row or Add Multiple Rows writes them. Cancellations can be a second automation.

steps.title: You connect Shopify and Google Sheets
steps.body: Connect both once and pick the spreadsheet and tab. Put your column headings in row one so each value lands in its column.

steps.title: An order comes in, rows appear
steps.body: Per order, you get one row with the items joined in a cell. Per item, each line gets its own row with the order number repeated.

steps.title: Your sheet keeps up with the shop
steps.body: Filter by item, total a day's sales, or hand the sheet to whoever packs the orders.

faqs.q: Should I use one row per order or one row per item?
faqs.a: One row per order suits daily totals. One row per item suits stock counts and best sellers, since you can filter by product or variant. Say which you want in your ask.

faqs.q: What happens when an order is cancelled?
faqs.a: Shopify has an Order Cancelled event. Build a second automation on it that finds the order's rows and marks them cancelled, so the totals stay honest.

faqs.q: What if the customer edits the items after ordering?
faqs.a: Shopify has an Order Line Items Are Edited event. A second automation on it can update the rows for that order. Without it, the sheet keeps the items from the moment the order was placed.

faqs.q: Can it only add paid orders?
faqs.a: Yes. New Order fires when an order is created, and Order Paid fires when it is paid. Tell Captain you want paid orders only.

faqs.q: Does it add my past orders?
faqs.a: No. It starts with the next order after you build it. For earlier ones, use Shopify's own export and paste the file into your sheet.

faqs.q: What does it cost to start?
faqs.a: 50agents is free to start. Tell Captain what you want, read the steps, and tap Build it.

faqs.q: What if a row is wrong or an order is missing?
faqs.a: The automation writes only to your own sheet, so you can fix any row by hand. Check that your headings sit in row one, and ask Captain to adjust the columns if a value lands in the wrong place.

faqs.q: Can I send orders to Airtable or WooCommerce instead?
faqs.a: A variation on this page writes to Airtable, and both Airtable and WooCommerce are in the catalog. Name your tools in your sentence to Captain.

faqs.q: How do I stop or change it?
faqs.a: Tell Captain what to change, such as paid orders only or a new column. Because it writes only to your sheet, a change never asks for approval.
